implementation.reference_algorithm: Dijkstra over the same versioned multigraph

contracts: A* uses Euclidean distance as an admissible heuristic because every edge cost must dominate its metric length.
Blocked runtime overlays exclude traversal without deleting structural edge identity.
Paths retain map_version, topology_version, localization_epoch, node IDs, edge IDs and metric polyline.
Smoothing accepts only shortcuts approved by an external swept-footprint validator.
Regulated pursuit uses body-frame lookahead, kappa=2*y_local/L^2 and bounded speed/yaw/lateral acceleration.
A candidate is not admitted across a stale lease generation, cancellation, map version or localization epoch.
Replacement activation invalidates older candidates before the new option can be admitted.
negative_cases: structurally unreachable goal raises instead of fabricating a path
invalid edge cost below metric length is rejected
smoothing cannot shortcut unless the swept validator approves
cancelled option cannot re-admit its candidate
old lease generation cannot win a replacement race
limitations: Final command authority remains in the existing supervisor/safety/mux chain; this package never publishes motor commands.
Stopping tubes, dynamic obstacle swept prediction, wheel calibration and physical braking evidence are not claimed by this SIL package.
The current pursuit generator is regulated-pursuit MVP; DWA arc search and nonholonomic swept validation remain future extensions.
A separate ROS public planner service was not introduced; the boundary is a typed in-process envelope as required by the architecture.
